title: Oxford Economics launches AskOE Business Foresight
gist: Oxford Economics launched AskOE Business Foresight, a conversational AI agent that links its proprietary economic indicators and forecasting methods directly to a client company's revenue drivers, extending its AskOE AI product suite (launched 2024) beyond general-purpose LLM tools by keeping model assumptions and data sources documented and traceable.

insights.claim: AskOE Business Foresight identifies the markets and economic indicators most closely linked to a company's historical performance, combines them into a tailored demand signal, and tests different forecasting approaches to find the method that best fits the business, all through a conversational interface requiring no specialist modeling skills.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: A no-code, conversational forecasting tool that ties company revenue to macro indicators lowers the skill barrier for corporate finance and strategy teams to run scenario analysis in-house rather than commissioning bespoke economic consulting engagements.
insights.quote: Business Foresight identifies the markets and economic indicators most closely linked to a company’s historical performance. It combines these drivers into a tailored demand signal before testing different forecasting approaches

insights.claim: Unlike general-purpose LLM tools, Business Foresight draws on Oxford Economics' proprietary economic intelligence and economist-developed mapping logic and forecasting approaches, with key assumptions, indicators, and model choices documented for user visibility.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: The explicit positioning against 'general-purpose LLM tools' signals Oxford Economics is betting that proprietary data plus documented methodology, not raw model capability, is the differentiator that will win enterprise forecasting business against generic AI copilots.
insights.quote: Unlike general-purpose LLM tools, Business Foresight draws on Oxford Economics’ proprietary economic intelligence and uses mapping logic and forecasting approaches developed by its economists.

themes.theme: Part of a broader AI product strategy

insights.claim: Business Foresight is the latest addition to a growing AI suite Oxford Economics has built since launching AskOE in 2024, which also includes the AskOE Executive Lens agent and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations letting clients bring Oxford Economics' intelligence into their existing AI workflows.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Adoption of MCP integrations shows a traditional economic-research firm actively plugging its proprietary data into the broader AI-agent ecosystem rather than building only a closed standalone product, a distribution strategy other data/analytics vendors may need to match.
insights.quote: This includes purpose-built AI agents such as AskOEAI Executive Lens, as well as Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that enable clients to bring Oxford Economics’ intelligence into the AI tools and workflows they already use.
insights.locator: Business Foresight is the latest addition

insights.claim: Oxford Economics frames its AI strategy as unlocking more value from decades of accumulated proprietary economic intelligence and expertise, rather than simply using AI to deliver existing information faster.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: This articulates a monetization thesis for incumbent data/research firms facing AI disruption: proprietary datasets and domain expertise built over decades become the defensible moat that AI wrapping alone can package into new, sellable products.
insights.quote: The opportunity for us is not simply to use AI to deliver information faster. It is to use technology to unlock more value from the economic intelligence and expertise we have built over decades.
